metadata.title: Concept Drift: Why Good Models Get Worse Over Time
metadata.factual_scope: Accessible standalone explanation of concept drift, data drift, monitoring, retraining decisions, and overfitting distinctions.
metadata.methodological_boundary: Data drift and concept drift are related but distinct; warning signs require investigation; not every performance drop is drift and not every distribution change requires retraining.
metadata.production_gate: Narrative and visual plan approved; 16:9 review rendering authorized; clean final master not authorized.

beats.narration_text: Hi, my name is Ushasvi Rachel, and this video is about concept drift and why machine-learning models can become less accurate over time. A model can be correct when it is trained and still become worse later, because deployment does not freeze the world around it.

shot.visual_intent: Integrated presenter introduction and training-to-later timeline.

beats.narration_text: A model may validate well under its original conditions, then become less reliable after deployment. That does not necessarily mean it was poorly built. It means production is another phase of the machine-learning lifecycle, and conditions must continue to be checked.

shot.visual_intent: Initial reliability versus later production reliability.

beats.narration_text: Concept drift occurs when the statistical relationship between model inputs and the target changes over time. The code and model parameters may be unchanged, while the environment being modeled changes. The old mapping from features to outcomes can therefore become less useful.

shot.visual_intent: Feature-to-target relationship diagram and concise definition.

beats.narration_text: Relationships can change for many reasons: customer behavior, seasonality, economic conditions, pricing, fraud tactics, platform changes, or new products and competitors. These are general possibilities, not evidence that any one factor caused a particular drift event.

shot.visual_intent: Balanced grid of general post-deployment change drivers.

beats.narration_text: Data drift and concept drift are related, but they are not identical. Data drift means the distribution of input features changes. Concept drift means the relationship between those inputs and the target changes. A feature shift may be worth investigating, but it does not automatically prove concept drift.

Consider a hypothetical model predicting which customers are likely to buy a product. During training, high website engagement may be strongly associated with purchases. Later, people may continue browsing frequently but purchase less because behavior, prices, or economic conditions changed.

shot.visual_intent: Hypothetical customer-purchase prediction pipeline and two periods.

beats.narration_text: In the training period, engagement and purchasing follow relationship A. In the later production period, they follow relationship B. The earlier pattern may no longer hold as strongly. Both periods can contain valid observations even though the relationship between feature and outcome changed.

shot.visual_intent: Before-and-after relationship graphics without numerical values.

beats.narration_text: This matters because the prediction service may continue operating normally while real-world performance quietly declines. There may be no software error or obvious failure. But not every performance drop is concept drift, so teams should investigate before assigning a cause.

shot.visual_intent: Healthy service status contrasted with declining usefulness.

beats.narration_text: Warning signs include declining production accuracy or other relevant metrics, shifts in feature distributions, changing error patterns, and performance differences across time periods or user groups. These are signals for investigation, not automatic diagnoses.

A reliable production system monitors model performance, feature distributions, predictions, outcomes, and errors over time. Teams compare periods and examine whether changes are concentrated in particular groups. Monitoring turns quiet degradation into something visible and auditable.

shot.visual_intent: Full-width post-deployment monitoring loop and dashboard cards.

beats.narration_text: When a change appears, diagnosis comes first. Teams investigate the cause, retrain when appropriate, and validate the updated model before deployment. Retraining is not automatically required whenever a feature distribution changes. The response should follow the evidence and the prediction setting.

shot.visual_intent: Investigate-to-retrain decision workflow and retraining guardrail.

beats.narration_text: Concept drift is also different from overfitting. Overfitting means the model learned its training data too specifically. Concept drift means the environment, or the input-to-target relationship, changed after training. Both can hurt generalization, but they are different problems with different diagnostic questions.

Good machine-learning systems therefore require ongoing monitoring after deployment. Training and validation establish how a model performs under known conditions; production monitoring checks whether those conditions still hold. A good model today is not guaranteed to be a good model tomorrow.

shot.visual_intent: Lifecycle timeline and final branded takeaway.
